BLOCKER: s3store.ApplyLifecycle applies retention (potentially irreversible COMPLIANCE) *before* validating the rest of the policy: mutual-exclusivity of LegalHold/ReleaseLegalHold and other arg checks happen afterwards, so an invalid request can permanently lock an object and then return an error — violating the package's own "one-way door, validate explicitly" contract. All policy validation must complete before any PutObjectRetention call.
MAJOR: objreconcile.Scan validates manifest keys with raw `strings.HasPrefix(e.Key, prefix)`; a prefix without a trailing slash ("p") accepts "pabc/x", so invalid/orphan classification is wrong at tenant boundaries. Normalize prefix and require `prefix + "/"` (or exact match) consistently.

s3store.Capabilities() hardcodes ObjectLock: true regardless of bucket configuration. Capability probing then lies for buckets without object lock (and for S3-compatible backends lacking the API), undermining the fail-closed design; detect or record bucket object-lock config at construction.

s3store lifecycle_integration_test applies GOVERNANCE retention of 1h then `defer st.Delete(...)`, which the owner cannot perform under governance retention: every run leaks a permanently retention-locked object in the bucket (compliance-governance garbage accumulation). Release retention or use a bypass/teardown path and assert the delete error.

s3store.Put with Immutable=true but Retention=0 is silently accepted — Immutable without any lock is a no-op, contradicting "PutOptions.Retention/Immutable are enforced or explicitly rejected per provider". Reject Immutable-only, or map it to a documented default retention.

objreconcile.notFound falls back to substring matching on error text ("not found", "nosuchkey"), which will misclassify arbitrary wrapped provider errors and turn infrastructure faults into reported "missing" drift. Require a typed sentinel from datastore adapters instead of message parsing.
MINOR: objpolicy.Mint logs only denies via stdlib `log.Printf` with raw key material (potential PII/tenant data in plaintext logs) and never audits successful mints; use structured, redacted audit logging for a privilege-boundary component.
s3store.ObjectLifecycle calls GetBucketVersioning on every per-object call — N+1 API calls and added latency when scanning many objects; cache versioning status (it is bucket-scoped).

objpolicy.cleanPath's `strings.Contains(c, "..")` is dead code (path.Clean on a "/"+-prefixed input never leaves ".."), giving false confidence in the traversal guard; keep the check but test the actual normalized output, and document that caller-supplied prefixes are silently rewritten.

objpolicy re-exports `ErrUnsupported = datastore.ErrUnsupported` under a second package name; consumers may create wrapping chains that confuse `errors.Is` reporting — prefer documenting the datastore sentinel directly.
objreconcile Report relies on slice lengths for counts; for large stores the JSON arrays are unbounded (no pagination/streaming or count fields), which limits operational scalability of the scanner.
Mint allows the key equal to the tenant prefix itself (k == prefix), minting URLs for the prefix/"directory" key; likely unintended — require a strictly deeper key.

New go.mod files declare `go 1.21` and use relative `replace` directives; align the Go toolchain version with the rest of the monorepo and confirm the replace convention matches existing modules (objstore, s3store).
NIT: Schema constant is `pf.objreconcile/2` in a brand-new package with no v1; start at /1 or document the versioning rationale.
AllowedMethods() exists solely for docs/tests while the allowlist is unexported and duplicated conceptually in S3/local providers; a single source of truth comment would help.
LifecyclePolicy.Mode uses magic strings "GOVERNANCE"/"COMPLIANCE" in the shared datastore package; export typed constants to prevent drift across providers.
retentionFor rejects Retention < 1 minute with an ad-hoc error rather than a package-level sentinel; typed errors would improve testability.
SUMMARY: Solid, on-standard work overall: optional capability interface with a fail-closed sentinel, a central signed-URL policy with allowlist/TTL/tenant guards, and a read-only deterministic reconcile scanner with meaningful tests — all in Go, no API surface change.

Top risks: the irreversible COMPLIANCE retention applied before full policy validation (blocker), prefix-boundary bug in orphan/invalid classification, hardcoded ObjectLock capability, and the S3 integration test leaking retention-locked objects.
Recommend fixing the validation-ordering and prefix issues before merge; add typed error sentinels for provider "not found" and structured audit logging in the policy boundary.
